newsitem.title: UK: European tobacco stocks hit by cancer link.
newsitem.headline: European tobacco stocks hit by cancer link.

text.p: European tobacco shares fell on Monday amid fears that new evidence to suggest a direct link between smoking and lung cancer could strengthen litigation against the tobacco giants.

Scientists in the United States said they had identified a substance in the tar of tobacco smoke that directly transforms human lung tissue. The findings, published in the prestigious Science journal on Friday, are the first direct link to be found between smoking and cancer.

Britain's B.A.T Industries, which is already heavily exposed to U.S. litigation through its Brown & Williamson unit, makers of Kent, Kool and State Express cigarettes, closed down 7 pence (11 cents) at 424p ($6.73) after hitting a low of 420p ($6.67). The shares have fallen dramatically since January, when they were valued at 580p ($9.20).

In France, shares in tobacco group Seita, makers of the Gitanes and Gauloises brands of cigarettes, lost almost 4 percent. In Spain, shares in the majority state-owned Tabacalera fell 2 percent on the latest findings.
